newsitem.title: USA: CSW considers options in El Paso case.
newsitem.headline: CSW considers options in El Paso case.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said on Friday that it is considering further legal options after a bankruptcy court judge ruled that it would have to pay El Paso Electric Co over a terminated merger agreement.
The two companies entered a merger agreement in May 1993, but it was later terminated June 1995, Central and South West said.

Judge Larry Kelly for the U.S. Bankruptcy Court ruled that Central and South West owes El Paso Electric the $25 million termination fee under terms of the merger agreement, Central and South West said.

Also, Judge Kelly ruled that Central and South West may owe El Paso Electric "interest-carry" costs, alleged by El Paso Electric to be approximately $18 million, the company said. The interest-carry issue specifically was reserved for later determination, Central and South West said.

The interim order also provides that, unless separately ordered by the court, neither Central and South West nor El Paso Electric can recover attorney fees or costs in the case from each other, Central and South West said.
